The module list saved in the same boot has one such line for each of its 12 modules [Ref43] .

Every state line holds the boot id 3bfc57a1-e235-4fe5-8c09-a94642f9b60b. The record of this boot, written at 20:02:21 UTC, shows 12 x "Configured Memory Speed: 7200 MT/s" [Ref42] .
The speed was not read during the rerun. Reading it needs root. Assumption, not measured: the speed does not change inside one boot.

Firmware settings other than the memory speed

Two TXREQ settings were changed for another test on 2026-11-17, at 03:43:50 and 04:05:38 UTC [Ref46] [Ref47] . Both were set back at 04:13:19 UTC to their values of the 8000 MT/s boot [Ref48] . The settings list saved after that is equal to the list of the 8000 MT/s boot in all 1490 entries (the order of the entries differs) [Ref49] [Ref50] . The only later change on record is DIMM Frequency = 7200 MT/s (file time 19:43:03 UTC) [Ref51] .

886 of the 1490 entries show no readable value in both lists (883 show ValueUnavailable, 3 show VStoreError). "On record" means the 4 files named set.txt in the results folder. Insufficient data: the firmware settings in the boot of the rerun, apart from the memory speed. No full list was saved in that boot. A settings list saved in that boot would resolve it (needs root).
The 8000 MT/s rows: one boot, 12 modules

The saved kernel log of that boot runs from 2026-11-09 21:20:15 to 2026-11-17 03:44:00 UTC and holds the line "This system has 12 DIMM sockets" [Ref52] . The number in this line is not the slot count of the board. The kernel log of the boot that started on 2026-11-17 04:17:19 UTC holds "This system has 10 DIMM sockets", and its memory size line shows 64 GiB less [Ref53] . Every 8000 MT/s process used here was launched inside the time of the kernel log of the 8000 MT/s boot. The settings list saved in that boot shows DIMM Frequency = 8000 MT/s [Ref49] .
No reading of the applied speed was saved in that boot.
Corrected hardware error records in the 8000 MT/s rows

Rows L-1 to L-4: the journal of the 8000 MT/s boot holds such records during two of the four rows: 2 during L-1, and 5 and 4 during the two processes of L-2. It holds 0 during L-3 and L-4 [Ref54] [Ref55] [Ref56] [Ref57] [Ref58] . Rows A-1 to A-3 (2026-11-13): the journal holds 4 records between the first launch of A-1 (18:17:21 UTC) and the launch that followed the last A-3 process used here (20:58:43 UTC). All 4 fall into A-2: 2 at 20:50:58 UTC, the second in which the bw_new read process of round 1 was launched, and 2 at 20:51:10 UTC, 2 s after the launch of a bw_new write process that this page does not use [Ref54] [Ref23] [Ref24] [Ref26] .
The data do not show that a record changed a rate. For the rerun the kernel log was not read (section 3).
The lowest asmread value of the 8000 MT/s pool comes from an interval with such records

The lowest asmread value of the pool L-1 to L-4 is 288.54 GB/s. 2 corrected hardware error records have the journal time 2026-11-15 18:54:52 UTC. This interval ran from about 18:54:51 to 18:54:55 UTC on the same day (est.: time of the launch line plus the seconds since the process start in the thread rows) [Ref54] [Ref28] [Ref56] . Without this one interval the pool spans 298.61 to 309.17 GB/s (10 intervals / 7 processes / 1 boot). Part L (321.65 to 327.93 GB/s, 6 intervals / 3 processes / 3 sessions / 1 boot) still lies above it, by 12.48 GB/s at the nearest ends.
The data do not show that the records lowered this interval. Both times have a resolution of 1 s.
